pezzi.36: They are not general principles: they are the rules that decide what goes into a system and what stays out.
pezzi.38: The deterministic part before the model.
pezzi.39: Nothing is declared done without a test.
pezzi.40: Better a visible error than a plausible, wrong answer.
pezzi.41: Every agent has only the permissions it needs.
pezzi.42: Client data stays with the client.
pezzi.43: A system counts if it stays standing over time, not on the day of the demo.
pezzi.45: The third month, not the day of the demonstration.
pezzi.46: From the manual process to the third month
pezzi.47: I start from the work someone does by hand today, with its exceptions. I build one small piece, with its check next to it. Then I watch how it holds up when the models change and people use it in ways nobody had foreseen.
pezzi.51: One small piece with its test
pezzi.55: If the first conversation makes it clear that the problem can be solved without agents, I say so. It happens, and finding out halfway through a project costs a great deal more.
pezzi.58: Tell me about the work you do by hand today: who does it, how often, and what happens when a piece of information is missing.
